intent: Provide the per-commit file-length gate that the shell-splitting work has been referring to. It did not exist: no check_file_length.sh was ever committed to this repo, so every split so far was checked by eye.
scope: Non-goal: wiring it into .pre-commit-config.yaml. 24 files are still over the cap, so a hook would block every commit. It lands as a hook once --all exits 0.
changes: New meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh enforcing a 250-line cap, taking either --all (every tracked file) or an explicit file list.
Scope is source extensions only (sh/bash/zsh, py, kt/kts, dart, ts/tsx/js/jsx). Markdown, HTML, JSON, YAML, lockfiles and .gitignore are excluded: a length cap on data and prose is noise.
third_party/ and docs/superpowers/ are excluded as vendored or generated trees.
Reports each violation with its line count and the overage, sorted worst-first, on stderr; exits 1 when anything is over.

verification.evidence: Reports exactly 24 files over the cap and exits 1. This independently reproduces the count carried in NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md (20 shell, 2 kotlin, 1 dart, plus the markdown brief which this scope correctly excludes), which is what confirms the extension scope matches the intended one.
'all checked files are within 250 lines', exit 0 — the gate passes its own cap at 135 lines.
'325  phone_focus_mode/dns_enforcer.sh (+75)', exit 1 — named-file mode reports the overage.
Both exit 0: the markdown is out of extension scope and the 302-line vendored script is under an excluded prefix.
'Error: pass --all or one or more file paths', exit 1 — no-argument invocation cannot be mistaken for a clean run.
Clean. An initial SC2155 on the readonly SCRIPT_NAME assignment was fixed by splitting declaration from assignment, not suppressed.

risks: The cap is a blunt measure: a 260-line file with one long data table is treated the same as a 260-line file with tangled control flow. The gate is an alarm, not a judgement.
Excluding docs/superpowers/ means generated evidence and contract artifacts are never capped. That is intended, but a genuinely oversized script placed there would go unchecked.
rollback: git revert the commit and delete the script; nothing depends on it yet because it is deliberately not wired into pre-commit.
After rollback, confirm pre-commit run --all-files still passes, which it will, since no hook references the script.
